claims.text: The student guidance allows use of generative AI tools as study aids for personal learning and research, while distinguishing that from submitting AI-generated output as the student's own assessment work.

claims.text: The researcher tool-selection guidance points researchers to University-approved Enterprise Microsoft Copilot access and tells them to confirm the Enterprise data protection indicator before using it.

evidence.quote: The University provides approved access to the Enterprise version of Microsoft Co-Pilot which you can access via your University account. claims.text: The AI tools licensing guidance tells users to review terms and conditions before registering for a new AI tool and to seek advice when data protection, accessibility, indemnity, or copyright concerns arise.

evidence.quote: Before registering for a new tool, it is crucial to review the Terms and Conditions (licence), which form the legal agreement between you and the supplier. If issues arise, such as non-compliance with accessibility or data protection standards, indemnification requirements, or copyright concerns, seek further guidance from your local licensing or IT procurement teams before registering for the service.
evidence.title: AI tools licensing review guidance

topics.summary: Retained research guidance places responsibility for substantive claims and outputs on human researchers and discusses endorsed tools. The DOCX was not independently recovered; these are scoped reference records.

claims.text: The research AI guidance applies to University of Birmingham researchers using, developing, or deploying AI, and places accountability for substantive claims, interpretations, and outputs on human researchers.

evidence.quote: This guidance applies to all researchers at the University of Birmingham who engage with Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the context of research, whether by using existing tools, developing new models, or deploying AI systems in real-world environments. A human researcher must be accountable for every substantive claim, interpretation, and output.
evidence.title: Guidance for the use of AI in research
evidence.location: Guidance for the use of AI in research - Scope and Human Oversight

claims.text: The research AI guidance says researchers should use University-endorsed AI tools for licensing, data protection, and information security compliance, and should justify and record use of unapproved or externally hosted tools.

evidence.quote: Researchers should use only University-endorsed AI tools to ensure compliance with licensing, data protection, and information security requirements. Use of unapproved or externally hosted tools should be justified and recorded in project documentation such as Data Management Plans or ethics submissions.
evidence.title: Guidance for the use of AI in research
evidence.location: Guidance for the use of AI in research - Transparency And Acknowledgment

claims.text: The University states that generative AI detection tools are not currently allowable and that student work should not be uploaded to generative AI detection software.
